established_findings.statement: LLM-based agents are being proposed and explored for NetOps/AIOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, diagnosis, limited remediation), but operational reliability depends heavily on surrounding orchestration, validators, and tool pipelines rather than the base LLM alone.
limitations: Primarily survey/architectural and prototype system reports rather than large-scale production deployments
Heterogeneous sources include preprints and engineering reports with variable empirical scope

established_findings.statement: Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) and similar generate–validate–repair architectures are a recurring recommended mitigation to make stochastic LLM outputs acceptable for deterministic or safety-critical artifacts (code, configs).
limitations: Evaluations are case studies or single-case proofs-of-concept; robustness across diverse NetOps tasks is not comprehensively demonstrated
Detection/repair effectiveness depends on available deterministic verifiers and the class of errors

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented agent frameworks (LLM + tool invocation / orchestration) improve capability for multi-step operational workflows but introduce new reliability modes (tool-selection, tool-schema mismatch, runtime/tool queueing) that require explicit runtime controls and verification policies.
limitations: Most evidence analyzes failures at the architectural/runtime level; empirical frequency/severity in production NetOps remains underreported
Work spans multiple domains (not exclusively networking), so some tool-failure modes are general

established_findings.statement: Hallucination/confabulation and reasoning failures in LLM outputs are well-documented and pose practical risks for actionable NetOps outputs; detection, calibration, and sequential verification strategies are active research directions.
limitations: Most detection/verification work evaluated on benchmarks or non-networking domains; direct NetOps-domain detection performance varies with available grounding data/tools
Terminology and taxonomy vary across studies (hallucination vs confabulation)

established_findings.statement: Constrained or schema-preserving output formats (DSLs, YANG profiles, structured decoding) increase syntactic/semantic reliability of model-generated configurations in controlled evaluations.
limitations: High syntactic accuracy in controlled tasks does not guarantee safe runtime semantics when applied to diverse vendor CLIs or live devices
Evaluations are lab-based with limited topology/device diversity

established_findings.statement: Existing literature and reviews identify a gap between analytical capability (detection/diagnosis) and evidence required to grant authority for autonomous changes in production systems; the production evidence for general autonomous action is weak.
limitations: Reviews synthesize available reports up to 2026; absence of evidence for broad autonomous authority is observational (lack of published production studies)
Specific regulated or safety-critical deployment evidence may exist but is not represented in the supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do LLM-generated, validator-approved configurations behave correctly on heterogeneous, vendor-specific live devices across realistic failure modes and adversarial inputs?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: motivation drawn from prototype/lab studies and review gaps
limitations: Existing evidence demonstrates lab/prototype success (YANG profile, MeshAgent) but does not settle heterogeneous live-device behavior under adversarial conditions

unresolved_questions.statement: How effective and cost-efficient are sequential, cost-aware verification policies (mixed verifiers, token-level drift detection) when deployed at NetOps scale under firm latency or operational-deadline constraints?
limitations: Proposals provide theoretical/trace-driven simulations; operational cost–latency tradeoffs in real NetOps pipelines remain empirically unresolved

unresolved_questions.statement: What standard evaluation metrics, datasets, and canary/rollback-aware protocols best capture operational safety and readiness for agentic NetOps actions?
limitations: Multiple papers call for such standards, but no single, widely adopted operational benchmark/protocol is evidenced among supplied records

unresolved_questions.statement: How robust are tool-selection and tool-registry mechanisms to deceptive or marketing-biased tool descriptions in NetOps agent ecosystems?
limitations: Registry evidence is cross-domain; NetOps-specific tool-market dynamics need domain-targeted study

candidate_gaps.statement: Lack of publicly available, provenance-rich NetOps datasets and testbeds that pair LLM-generated configurations with deterministic verifier outcomes and (sandboxed) execution traces for reproducible evaluation.
limitations: Some projects provide lab/topology artifacts (YANG profile) but comprehensive provenance-rich datasets coupling generation/verification/execution are not evident in supplied records

candidate_gaps.statement: Insufficient operational evaluation of GVR/verify-repair loops integrated with network verifiers (Batfish/VeriFlow/HSA) across diverse vendor CLIs and real-world topology/failure distributions.
limitations: Architectural proposals argue for integration; concrete cross-vendor empirical studies are not present in the record set

candidate_gaps.statement: Absence of standardized, canary/rollback-aware scoring metrics that reflect operational risk (e.g., verification coverage, rollback-success rate, real-time abstention utility) for agentic NetOps.
limitations: Papers recommend such metrics but do not converge on a single standard set or provide broad empirical validation

candidate_gaps.statement: Need for reproducible auditing/preregistration practices and automated claim–evidence mapping for agentic NetOps experiments (provenance, hashes, execution manifests) to support trustworthy claims.
limitations: Protocol proposals exist; community adoption and toolchains for automated audit remain emergent

candidate_gaps.statement: Limited published evidence on the impact of distribution shift, adversarial prompts, or backdoor attacks specifically on NetOps-oriented agentic LLM pipelines.
limitations: Adversarial/backdoor work covers agentic systems generally; explicit NetOps-domain empirical attacks/exploit studies are scarce in supplied records

excluded_claims: LLMs alone (without validators, toolchains, and orchestration) are sufficient for safe autonomous network configuration deployment.

There is published, reproducible production evidence that general-purpose LLM agents can be granted autonomous write authority over live, heterogeneous network infrastructure without additional safeguards.
Existing constrained-generation or DSL approaches guarantee semantic correctness on all vendor devices in production.
No significant failure modes exist beyond those documented in general LLM agent literature.
